chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Fadl ibn al-Mubarak from al-Fadl ibn Yunus who said:

When Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) had lunch with me, and the washing tray was brought, he (peace be upon him) was given precedence, and he was in the center of the gathering, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Begin with the one on your right.' So when one had performed ablution, the slave intended to raise the tray, so Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Leave it, and wash your hands in it.'

key_terms.تَغَدَّى: had lunch / had the midday meal
key_terms.صَدْرِ الْمَجْلِسِ: the center / front of the gathering

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic etiquette for washing hands before eating according to the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated from Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him), establishes the etiquette of pre-meal ablution (wudu al-ta'am), emphasizing the protocol of serving the person on the right first. It further demonstrates the permissibility of using the same water used for pre-meal ablution for washing hands afterwards, rather than discarding it immediately, highlighting the virtue of avoiding waste (israf) in daily practices.
